It holds the Pet Directory and Program Manager, and its tools are the System Map and Startup Star. Astra’s PetOS is a platform that runs on Windows, not an operating system. nodes.name: The vet-clinic (community tickets)
nodes.job: Is your pet sick? A public issue tracker on GitHub: a farmer opens a ticket (vet-clinic-ticket-NNNN) with the sick tool’s code and error, after name-eraser and the secret scan; other farmers diagnose it and may offer a cure (a code fix). One tier below Kennel-verified: every community answer carries a warning and never runs by itself; a cure goes through quarantine, a checker agent and the farm’s L4. Every ticket is logged, and cures that work for many farms become official patches (PET-PROGRAM-FRAMEWORK.md, section 10). Outside the harness, like the Kennel.

nodes.name: The Shed (community tools and tricks)
nodes.job: Public, like the Kennel but for tools and tricks made by other creators (findastra/the-shed). Everything there is untrusted until it is quarantined, checked and approved by a farm’s L4. Trust tiers: official, Shed-verified, community (with a warning). Outside the harness.

A pet comes in from the farm’s own list of pets with every pet it requires; a pet that others on the farm require is not taken away without --with-dependents. plan shows it first and changes nothing; --yes does it. Since 2026-10-22 (Part 5b) it also adds a pet pack: every file is checked against the pet’s own repo on GitHub at the pack’s commit (a pack it cannot check comes in only with --unchecked), and the pet’s code goes into its own folder next to the farm, never run by itself. It writes only the farm’s pets.json, draft list, farm lock and those code folders, never anything on GitHub, and on a hub copy, whose pets change by pull request, it only checks and records (scripts/farm-pets-20261021.mjs, scripts/farm-pets-packs-20261022.mjs).

nodes.name: Face recorder
nodes.label: the-astral-plane-v1.0-face-recorder-v1.0
nodes.job: A tool of The Astral Plane (Astra, 2026-11-03: "I want to track my own face tracking data and my reaction to other people or scenarios"): records Astra's own face and eye values (VRCFaceTracking's parameters, as VRChat's OSC output repeats them) into a session file that stays on her PC, and a line she types marks a moment. Each recording adds to VRChat AI Astra, the copy of Astra. Other players named in VRChat's log get made-up names (pseudonymization; Astra: "just change the names so we know it's the same person, but not use their actual name"): Player- and 6 hex digits from a keyed hash with this PC's own salt, the same for the same person, never a real name or user ID; --no-pseudonyms keeps event types only. In code: it listens on 127.0.0.1 only and sends nothing of its own; it keeps only face, eye and tracking values (an optional relay, off unless asked, passes each packet on to VRChat unchanged, from a socket bound to 127.0.0.1). Only one app at a time can listen on VRChat's output, port 9001 on this PC, so the recorder shares it with other OSC apps such as OSCGoesBrrr through OSCQuery or an OSC router (a step on Astra's PC, not done yet). Merged into the-astral-plane main with Astra's OK on 2026-11-03 (face/ai_astra_face_recorder.py, 56 unit tests); never run against live VRChat, VRCFaceTracking or a real headset. Face-out is a preview only and not built.

nodes.name: Face Codec
nodes.label: the-astral-plane-v1.0-face-codec-v1.0
nodes.job: A tool of The Astral Plane (Astra, 2026-11-03: "Face codec is fine"): the Face Codec, how a whole face is written down, a layer on top of VRCFaceTracking's Unified Expressions. Its encoder turns one moment of Astra's face (Unified Expressions or VRCFT v2 values) into a face frame of 13 signals and plain words AI Astra's model can read ("smiling a lot, eyebrows raised, looking left"), never an emotion label; its decoder turns signals back into Unified Expressions weights, as a preview only. Face-out may change face and eye shapes only (Astra's decision 7, 2026-11-03: the Unified Expressions face shapes, the eyes and gaze; no toggles, no outfits). In code: no network or connector code, so it cannot send anything, and the decoder keeps only the 102 face and eye shapes (FACE_OUT_ALLOWED). Merged into the-astral-plane main with Astra's OK on 2026-11-03 (face/ai_astra_face_codec.py, 25 unit tests); never run against live VRChat, VRCFaceTracking or a real headset. Face-out is a preview only and not built.

nodes.job: A tool of The Astral Plane (Astra, 2026-11-03: "convert that into how the AI should be reacting in VR chat"): cuts Astra's reaction clips (0.5 to 3 s) out of her recorded sessions, after each moment she marked or each event, into a reaction book on her PC that she can review, rate good or bad and delete from. The book is VRChat AI Astra, the copy of Astra (Astra: "It's basically a copy of me"). Given a moment in words, it picks one of her closest reaction clips and varies it by at most 10%. It reads back only made-up names (Player- and 6 hex digits) and ignores anything else in that field; a session file it cannot read is skipped with the reason. In code: a preview only, with no way to send to VRChat; face-out, when it is built, may change face and eye shapes only (decision 7, 2026-11-03). Merged into the-astral-plane main with Astra's OK on 2026-11-03 (face/ai_astra_reactions.py, 25 unit tests); never run against live VRChat, VRCFaceTracking or a real headset.

nodes.job: A tool of The Astral Plane (Astra, 2026-11-03: "truly random quantum bits and vary her small mood shifts"): random bits for AI Astra's small variations, from a coin jar of bits measured on a real quantum computer (each used once), or from her PC's own random numbers when the jar is empty, and it says which. Her PC's own random numbers are already enough for this: the jar is an experiment. Also gentle, human-shaped noise for mood drift and blinks, with hard limits in code. A separate script fills the jar with Astra's own IBM Quantum account; it checks the jar before it signs in, and it has not been run. Merged into the-astral-plane main with Astra's OK on 2026-11-03 (face/ai_astra_quantum_coin.py, 27 unit tests, with stand-ins for Qiskit); never run against live VRChat, VRCFaceTracking or a real headset. This tool edits the app’s private chat records instead, whose format can change with any app update, so it runs only with Claude closed, backs every file up first, changes only the fields that say where a chat lives, refuses a file it does not recognise, and has an undo. It also renames Claude’s history folders so the chats’ histories and memory notes follow. Dry run unless told to apply. Its records step has only ever run on copies of the records.

It walks Temp itself and does not ask Everything, because a shell started by a Claude chat sees that app’s private copy of Local app data merged over the real one. nodes.job: A tool of The Farm (GitHub Goldfish's from 2026-10-14; The Farm's since 2026-11-08, Astra: "All recommended"): the Flash Audit, the checklist every pet is onboarded and reviewed with. On The Farm's page it is a tool box with its 71 checks as tools. The page checks follow the Model Pet Program, one per part of the template, and every build compares every pet program page with it (scripts/flash-template-20261112.mjs, Astra 2026-11-12); the others show the last run over every pet program, and Run asks the Flash Audit helper on this PC to run it again. The read-only auditor checks 18 of them by itself and writes an evidence ledger; GitHub Goldfish keeps the checks about words on GitHub (A15, A31, A57) (docs/flash-audit-20261014.md, scripts/idle-flash-audit-20261017.mjs, scripts/flash-audit-helper-20261108.mjs).

nodes.name: project-image-generator
nodes.label: github-aquarium-v1.0-project-image-generator-v1.0
nodes.job: A tool of GitHub Aquarium (GitHub Goldfish, 2026-10-17): finds the best pictures already in every public repo, optionally screenshots each live site with a browser already on the PC, writes one manifest and reports Flash Audit A55. Read only on GitHub; Portfolio Puffer uses it by grant (github-goldfish scripts/project-image-generator-20261017.mjs).

nodes.name: naming-corrections
nodes.label: github-aquarium-v1.0-naming-corrections-v1.0
nodes.job: A tool of GitHub Aquarium (GitHub Goldfish, 2026-10-08): remembers the naming corrections the owner asks for, one repo at a time (repo, mistaken name, preferred name), and flags the mistaken name in later audits. Rules stay in the browser or a private file outside Git, never in the repo (github-goldfish index.html, Remember correction).

nodes.name: never-say-checker
nodes.label: github-aquarium-v1.0-never-say-checker-v1.0
nodes.job: A tool of GitHub Aquarium (GitHub Goldfish, 2026-10-07): the owner’s own list of words that must never appear in public text; the Blatant check flags each one it finds. The list stays in the browser (github-goldfish index.html).

nodes.name: report-exporter
nodes.label: github-aquarium-v1.0-report-exporter-v1.0
nodes.job: A tool of GitHub Aquarium (GitHub Goldfish, 2026-10-07): copies the current audit report or downloads it as Markdown, to paste into a chat or a handoff card (github-goldfish index.html, Copy and Download).

nodes.name: achievement-tracker
nodes.label: github-aquarium-v1.0-achievement-tracker-v1.0
nodes.job: A tool of GitHub Aquarium (Astra, 2026-10-17: "it helps me track my GitHub achievements, lists suggestions on how to get the rest in order of easiest next"): estimates GitHub achievements from public GitHub data, ranks the easiest next ones, lets the owner set what the profile really shows, and offers Start Project ideas for her cyber security, AI and nomad course tracks. Built on github-goldfish branch claude/achievements-20261017, not merged yet.

nodes.name: findastra-readme-auditor
nodes.label: github-aquarium-v1.0-findastra-readme-auditor-v1.0
nodes.job: A tool of GitHub Aquarium (Codex, 2026-10-15): audits and revises the owner’s GitHub profile README with a local maker and checker, then waits for her review before it pushes a branch. Built on github-goldfish codex branches, not merged yet.

nodes.name: document-control-checker
nodes.label: github-aquarium-v1.0-document-control-checker-v1.0
nodes.job: A tool of GitHub Aquarium (GitHub Goldfish, 2026-10-07): the Document control check. Finds required files that are missing, malformed or uncontrolled: no README or LICENSE, a pet repo without pet.json, the pet-app topic or the credit line, a committed .env, stray copies such as "... (1).txt". Read only (github-goldfish index.html).

nodes.name: blatant-checker
nodes.label: github-aquarium-v1.0-blatant-checker-v1.0
nodes.job: A tool of GitHub Aquarium (GitHub Goldfish, 2026-10-07): the Blatant check. Finds plain errors a visitor can see: links to repos, files or #anchors that go nowhere, doubled words, typos, garbled characters, leftover TODOs, a token or personal folder path in public text, and any word on the never-say list. Read only (github-goldfish index.html).

nodes.name: organizational-checker
nodes.label: github-aquarium-v1.0-organizational-checker-v1.0
nodes.job: A tool of GitHub Aquarium (GitHub Goldfish, 2026-10-07): the Organizational check. Finds things in the wrong place or named off-pattern: default branch not main, "Moved:" stubs not archived, no topics, a README title that does not echo the repo name, a profile line that disagrees with the repo's description, old pet words. Read only (github-goldfish index.html).

nodes.name: systemic-checker
nodes.label: github-aquarium-v1.0-systemic-checker-v1.0
nodes.job: A tool of GitHub Aquarium (GitHub Goldfish, 2026-10-07): the Systemic check. Finds patterns across the whole account: mixed apostrophes and dashes, mixed description style, some repos licensed and some not, a pet missing from the registry. Read only (github-goldfish index.html).

nodes.name: showcase-checker
nodes.label: github-aquarium-v1.0-showcase-checker-v1.0
nodes.job: A tool of GitHub Aquarium (GitHub Goldfish, 2026-10-19, at Astra's request): the Showcase check and panel. For every project the profile README advertises, it names its kind (VRChat world, Unity asset library, Discord project, website, pet …) and checks the README shows what that kind should: for a world, what's in it, how to visit, what's being built now and what's missing; plus the last commits and open pull requests. The homepage is the shop window, each README is what's on the shelf. Read only. In github-goldfish index.html (PR #19, merged 2026-10-19).

nodes.name: outstanding-items
nodes.label: github-aquarium-v1.0-outstanding-items-v1.0
nodes.job: A tool of GitHub Aquarium (Astra, 2026-10-21: "Can we get the GitHub goldfish to check the outstanding items on GitHub?", then all recommended, github-goldfish card 006): what waits on the farm owner on GitHub, from every repo they own, read only and sorted by the merge-order rank: jobs failing on a main branch, pull requests ready for her OK, handoff cards that wait on her, conflicts, failing checks and stacked pull requests for their chats, branches with work and no pull request, and pull requests nobody has touched for a month (close?). It runs when asked (npm run outstanding-items, or a chat before a merge chart) and writes the list for this page's panel and the Pets Board on her PC only, because it names private repos. The Pets Board's GitHub reading moved here (scripts/outstanding-items-20261021.mjs).

nodes.name: close-or-keep

nodes.job: An important tool of GitHub Aquarium (Astra, 2026-10-29: "All of those things are tools", then "make these important tools for the goldfish"): one of the five groups outstanding-items sorts, in the merge-order rank. nodes.name: Pets Board
nodes.label: github-aquarium-v1.0-pets-board-v1.0

nodes.name: red-jobs
nodes.label: github-aquarium-v1.0-red-jobs-trick-v1.0
nodes.job: A trick of GitHub Aquarium (github-goldfish skills/red-jobs/SKILL.md; Astra, 2026-10-22, sharing paper-girl’s Actions page: "add a skill to the goldfish that corresponds to this"): read a GitHub Actions job that fails on a main branch, name its cause from the causes seen so far (a private repo’s Pages, a private checkout, a changed input, a failing test, a workflow file), and hand Astra the one next step with its link: her own click, a chat’s fix or a slide deck. Read only; it never switches a workflow, reruns a job or changes a repo. Uses only outstanding-items.

nodes.label: file-master-v1.0-mass-delete-v1.0

It never hard-deletes: it plans, waits for Astra, then moves the items to _to_delete with an undo manifest; other pets use it only with a grant. Its rules are in code (scripts/mass-delete-guard-20261016.mjs in the hub); the tool itself is not built.

nodes.name: fit-any-screen
nodes.label: mirror-pool-v1.0-fit-any-screen-v1.0
nodes.job: A tool of Mirror Pool (Platform Platypus; Astra, 2026-10-19: "make sure that this web page can be viewed from any device ... if you turn the device sideways, it rotates ... you can stretch it out and drag the corners"): a script a page includes so it fills any screen. It follows rotation, window resizing and the browser's own bars, keeps clear of a notch, keeps a canvas within what a phone's browser can draw, asks for full screen without ever waiting on the answer, and keeps the screen awake. Learned from the Pocket Message Board (platform-platypus tools/fit-any-screen/fit-any-screen-20261019.js).

nodes.name: fit-check
nodes.label: mirror-pool-v1.0-fit-check-v1.0
nodes.job: A tool of Mirror Pool (Platform Platypus): measures a page on 19 screens (phones, iPads and computer windows; phones and iPads also on their side) in a headless Edge or Chrome pretending to be each device, loaded fresh and turned or resized live, for sideways scrolling, gaps in a full-screen page and canvases that were not redrawn. It only reads; the page is served on this PC only (platform-platypus tools/fit-check/fit-check-20261019.mjs). First run: the Pocket Message Board, 19 of 19 screens fit, 2026-10-19.

nodes.name: device-shots
nodes.label: mirror-pool-v1.0-device-shots-v1.0

nodes.name: page-check
nodes.label: mirror-pool-v1.0-page-check-v1.0
nodes.job: A tool of Mirror Pool (Platform Platypus; Astra, 2026-11-11: its pet program on the model of Wonderland Launchpad, its tool working on the page): the page checker from findastra/platform-platypus index.html. Check a page shows a pasted or opened page on iPhone SE, iPhone 16 Pro, Pixel 9, Galaxy S24, iPad mini and a desktop at their screen sizes, with their bars and notches drawn on, measures sideways scrolling, tap targets, small text, iPhone input zoom and content under the notch, and reads its code for cross-platform mistakes; Compare screenshots shows where two platforms' screenshots differ; Sites I watch lists Astra's pages and what each still needs. It runs in this browser and sends nothing anywhere (apps/platform-platypus-page-check-20261111.html).
nodes.does: Shows a page on six phones, an iPad and a desktop at once, says what to fix, and compares screenshots.

nodes.name: make-a-page-fit-any-screen

nodes.job: A trick of Mirror Pool (platform-platypus skills/make-a-page-fit-any-screen/SKILL.md): give a page what it needs to fit any screen, run fit-check on every screen, look at the device-shots contact sheet, publish, add the page to Sites I watch, and ask Astra for the real-device check. Uses only fit-any-screen, fit-check and device-shots.
